confirmed.title: With Up next open, Tab keeps loading more Up next, so Comments takes 188 Tabs to reach
confirmed.where: YouTube watch page (watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ), Up next section open, Comments closed, keyboard only
confirmed.evidence: I loaded the page fresh, focused the Up next summary, pressed Enter, then pressed Tab with 150 ms between presses (scratchpad t1r8/tabgrow.ts). Up next grew as focus moved through it: 40 items after 20 Tabs, 60 after 40, 100 after 60, 139 after 100, 157 after 140, 175 after 160 and 187 after 180. The Comments summary was reached only after 188 Tabs, once YouTube ran out of related videos. Before that, in a kb.ts walk, 250 Tabs from the Up next summary never reached Comments: Up next ended at 178 items, the same as the original's 178. In round 7 (works.md line 61, Tab order 'Up next, Comments, Sort, reply buttons'), Up next stayed at 20, so Comments came about 21 Tabs after it. In the original, ytd-comments comes before #secondary #related in the DOM (compareDocumentPosition: commentsBeforeRelated=true), so a keyboard user reaches the comments first. The only way around it is to Shift+Tab back to the Up next summary and close the section.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1; SIFT_PORT=9461 ./scripts/chrome.sh start; SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/t1r8/tabgrow.ts (it loads watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ, opens Up next with Enter, and presses Tab up to 200 times, printing the Up next size every 20 Tabs and the Tab count when the Comments summary gets focus).
confirmed.suspectedCause: This comes from the F722 fix. youtube.loadMore() in src/content/adapters/youtube.ts now uses the Up next continuation whenever Comments is closed (store sec:comments !== true). Focus moving to the last Up next link scrolls Sift's view to its end, and that seems to trigger loadMore, so each pass adds about 20 more before focus can leave the section. Leads: do not load more because of a focus move (only on End or a scroll by the reader), or let Up next load more through an explicit 'More' control, or put Comments before Up next, as the original's order does.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced 3 times with the reporter's tabgrow.ts on my own tab: fresh watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ, Up next opened with Enter, Tab every 150 ms. Up next grew as focus moved through it in every run. Two runs needed 191 and 189 Tabs to reach the Comments summary, with Up next growing 20 to 40, 60, 100, 120, 139, 178, then 190 or 188. One run stopped growing at 40 and reached Comments after 41 Tabs. The code matches: the host scroll listener in src/content/index.ts (around lines 2324-2346) calls loadMore() whenever Sift's view is within 1.5 screens of its end. The reader does not have to have scrolled. With Comments closed, youtube.loadMore() (src/content/adapters/youtube.ts, around line 1102) picks the Up next continuation. So each focus move onto the last links loads 20 more. Up next and Comments both start collapsed, so this hits a keyboard user who opened Up next. They cannot Tab past it until YouTube runs out of related videos. Medium fits. I did not check whether this is a regression.
confirmed.fix: In the host scroll listener in src/content/index.ts, do not call loadMore() for a scroll caused by focus. Skip it when the last input was Tab or Shift+Tab, or when the scroll came right after a focusin, and keep it for wheel, touch, End, PageDown and scrollbar scrolling. Or give the Up next items block an explicit 'more' control (Block.more) built in the watch() code of src/content/adapters/youtube.ts, and stop youtube.loadMore() from loading Up next on scroll alone.

confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice on watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&persist_hl=1&hl=es (lang=es-ES, UI fully Spanish). I compared each Up next line with the original's titles. Run 1: lines 2-4 were Spanish rewrites ('Boney M. interpreta «Rasputin»...', 'Metallica interpreta «Fade to Black» en Sphere...'). The other 15 rewrites were English ('Daryl Hall & John Oates perform “Maneater”', 'Michael Jackson performs “Billie Jean” live at Madison Square Garden...'). Even the Japanese titles came out in English ('Hatsune Miku sings the original song “LEGENDS”', 'Ado song “Patient A”'). Run 2 had the same pattern: lines 2-4 Spanish, then 16 English rewrites. The reporter saw the reverse split (mostly Spanish), but the effect is the same: one list in two languages. That breaks the design comment in doLines and listLang, which promise one language for the whole list. The code supports the suspected cause. In doLines (src/background/index.ts lines 492-495), pc.lang is stored only for a batch of 4 or more items. A first batch of 3 decides by itself, and the next batch decides again. The 3-then-rest split I saw fits that. I did not re-check the search page, to save AI calls. I reset hl=en afterwards.
confirmed.fix: In doLines in src/background/index.ts, store pc.lang from the first batch of any size, at least when knownLang(req.lang) is set. Every later batch on the page then reuses that one decision. Also make listLang/entryLang in src/background/text.ts keep the page language for a small sample unless the titles are clearly in another language.

confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. The Short version's first paragraph is 'Donald Trump calificó de “fraudulentas” las elecciones de Brasil, pero no presentó pruebas.' In the full text, /fraudulentas/ is false. The source says '“fraude”' and 'parece que es otro fraude electoral' and 'amañadas'. confirmed.title: Guardian article: Play on the video does nothing, and nothing says why
confirmed.evidence: Sift shows the video poster and a 'Play' button. Clicking it adds no iframe or video to the original's youtube-overlay block (innerHTML 6141 before and after; overlay button still there). The original page sits behind a full-screen 'It's your choice' cookie consent wall (Sourcepoint iframe). Its YouTube overlay also does nothing when clicked from a script while that wall is up. Sift hides the wall, so a Sift user has no way to unlock the video. I did not click any consent button (it records a choice), so I have not verified that consent makes the video play on the original. Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r8t2-guardian-video-play.png, /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r8t2-guardian-video-orig2.png
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun scripts/act.ts goto:<url> wait:9000 'eval:(()=>{window.__c=document.querySelector("[data-testid^=youtube-overlay-y7G]").closest("figure");return window.__c.innerHTML.length})()' click:Play wait:7000 'eval:[window.__c.innerHTML.length,[...window.__c.querySelectorAll("iframe")].length]' gives the same length and 0 iframes.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The consent wall is treated as noise, but here it gates a needed action. Sift could keep the site's reject/accept choice reachable when a gated control is used, or say that the site asks for a cookie choice first.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on both videos. Sift's 'Play' does nothing: the figure's innerHTML stays 6141 (then 5982/5983 on the second video), there are 0 iframes or videos, the youtube-overlay is still there, and no YouTube chunk or API loads. Sift shows no message about it. The original sits behind the Sourcepoint 'It's your choice' wall (html.sp-message-open, TCF eventStatus 'cmpuishown', gdprApplies true), which also locks scrolling: body overflow hidden, scrollHeight 900, wheel leaves scrollY at 0. I found a second cause the claim missed. Both players are <gu-island name=YoutubeBlockComponent deferuntil=visible> at y=2247 and 4122. They only hydrate when they scroll into view in the original, and Sift never scrolls the original, so the overlay has no handler yet. So a Sift user can neither make the cookie choice (No, thank you / Yes, I accept) nor get the player to hydrate. Not verified: that playback works after a choice. Like the claimant, I did not record a consent choice.
confirmed.fix: In generic.ts, the consent-wall branch (~line 6071, 'const wall = !!ctx.bare && consentWall(d, text)') should also keep the CMP as a dialog when it locks the page (html.sp-message-open, or body overflow hidden with a CMP iframe over the viewport), with the reject choice first. In proxy.ts or portal.ts, before replaying a click on a facade, scroll its original element into view (or into the top layer) and wait for hydration, so deferuntil=visible islands load. If the click still changes nothing, say so.
